sections.label: Casino crime and gambling rates
sections.summary: In 2023, 0.2% of reported crime cases occurred in casinos, and resident problem gambling rates stayed around 1%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In 2023, only 0.2% of all reported crime cases took place in the casinos.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The probable pathological and problem gambling rates among our residents also remain low and stable, at around 1%.

sections.label: Casino regulation bill aims
sections.summary: The Bill aims to enhance casino regulatory effectiveness, tighten regulation, strengthen protection for vulnerable groups, and regularise entry levies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: First, to enhance the operational effectiveness and future readiness of our casino regulatory regime; second, it tightens the regulation of casinos and licensees; third, it strengthens protection for vulnerable groups of people; and fourth, it regularises the entry levies collected from 4 April to 7 May 2024.

sections.label: GRA approval for casino betting
sections.summary: The GRA has no plans to allow casinos to offer betting or lotteries, but amendments require GRA approval before they can.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: To be clear, the GRA has no plans for now to allow casinos to offer betting or lotteries, but the amendments would make clear that the casinos would need GRA's approval before they can do so.

sections.label: GRA suitability decisions
sections.summary: The view is that the GRA is better-placed to make these regulatory decisions, in line with its responsibility for casino licensee suitability.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Our view is that the GRA is better-placed to make these decisions, as these are regulatory decisions in line with GRA's existing responsibility to ensure the suitability of casino licensees and their associates.

sections.label: New CCA offences
sections.summary: The Bill introduces three new offences in the CCA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces three new offences in the CCA.

sections.label: EP gambling liability
sections.summary: Clause 42 makes an EP liable for entering, remaining, or gambling on casino premises if he knows or ought to know he was an EP.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: To address this, clause 42 makes an EP liable for entering, remaining, or taking part in gambling on the casino premises, if it is proven that he knows or ought reasonably to know that he was an EP.

sections.label: Casino licensee suitability criteria expanded
sections.summary: Clause 5 expands suitability criteria for casino licensees, allowing the GRA to consider two additional criteria for ongoing suitability.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: To make clear our regulatory expectations, clause 5 expands the suitability criteria for casino licensees, to allow the GRA to consider two additional criteria when assessing a casino operator's suitability to hold a casino licence on an ongoing basis.

sections.label: Family Visit Limit breach criminalised
sections.summary: Clauses 3 and 42 criminalise breach of a Family Visit Limit, making breach of any Exclusion Order or Visit Limit an offence except self-imposed ones.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: To ensure that the Family Visit Limit acts as an effective protection for vulnerable persons, clauses 3 and 42 will criminalise the breach of a Family Visit Limit.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: With this amendment, the breach of any Exclusion Order or Visit Limit under the CCA, except those that are self-imposed, would constitute an offence.

sections.label: Regularising excess entry levy collection
sections.summary: About $4.4 million more than lawful entry levy rates was collected from 4 April to 7 May 2024, and clause 95 will regularise this amount.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: From 4 April to 7 May 2024, we collected about $4.4 million more than the lawful entry levy rates at that point in time, that is, the previous, lower entry rates.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Clause 95 will regularise this amount collected during that period.

sections.label: Excluded persons liable for casino gambling
sections.summary: The Bill makes an excluded person liable for entering, remaining or gambling on casino premises if he knows or ought reasonably to know he was excluded.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In particular, the Bill makes an excluded person liable for entering, remaining or taking part in gambling on the casino premises, if it is proven that he knows or ought reasonably to know that he was an excluded person.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: This places the responsibility on an individual to ensure that he is not excluded before entering or when remaining in the casino, where there are circumstances in which the individual ought reasonably to know that he is an excluded person.

sections.label: Criminalising Family Visit Limit breach
sections.summary: The Bill criminalises breach of a Family Visit Limit, so breach of any Exclusion Order or Visit Limit under the CCA is an offence except self-imposed ones.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Bill will tighten our regime by criminalising the breach of a Family Visit Limit, such that the breach of any Exclusion Order or Visit Limit under the CCA, except those that are self-imposed, will constitute an offence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: To conclude, our strict but pragmatic approach to regulating casino gambling has delivered good outcomes so far.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: This Bill will allow us to keep the casinos free from criminal influence, ensure gambling is conducted honestly and minimise the harm from gambling. : Mdm Deputy Speaker, I beg to move.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to statistics by MHA, casino-related crimes constitute just 0.2% of all crimes reported in Singapore.

sections.label: GRA scope over gambling activities
sections.summary: The Bill gives the GRA scope to regulate all casino gambling activities, including prescribing wagering instruments, but chance-based loot boxes are not regulated as gambling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I therefore support the Bill's proposal to future-proof our regulatory ambit by providing the GRA with the scope to regulate the entire suite of gambling activities in the casinos, including the ability to prescribe any instrument or thing to be considered as a wagering instrument.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: But Madam, our authorities currently do not regulate chance-based loot boxes as gambling as long as there are no in-game monetisation facilities.

sections.label: Family Visit Limits and Exclusion Orders
sections.summary: Family Visit Limits apply when families worry about gambling affliction, and NCPG may substitute Exclusion Orders with Visit Limits and vice versa.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Family Visit Limits are applied when family members are worried about their loved one's potential affliction by gambling and it makes sense to align the breach of these limits to existing Exclusion Orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I also fully support the proposal to provide the NCPG and its committees with the operational flexibility to immediately substitute an Exclusion Order with a Visit Limit and vice versa to protect individuals struggling with curbing their reliance on and addiction to gambling.

sections.label: Lowered Payment Threshold Amounts
sections.summary: Threshold amounts for payments out and receipts of money will be lowered to $4,000 from $10,000 and $5,000 respectively.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For both payments out and receipts of money in, the threshold amount will be lowered to $4,000, which is down from the current $10,000 for payments out and $5,000 for payments in.

sections.label: Electronic Information-Sharing Scheme for Casinos
sections.summary: Clause 47 establishes a new electronic information-sharing scheme for casino operators.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under clause 47, there will be a new electronic information-sharing scheme for casino operators.

sections.label: Casino Operator Fined for Due Diligence
sections.summary: A casino operator was fined $2.25 million for failing due diligence checks on deposits into patrons' accounts in prior years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For instance, it was reported in December last year that one of the casino operators was fined a total of $2.25 million for failing to perform due diligence checks on deposits into patrons' accounts in prior years.

sections.label: Increased Punishments and Jail Terms
sections.summary: Some fine-only offences become punishable by jail of up to three or seven years, and the speaker asks whether fines alone are insufficient.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The increases in punishments are very significant and it is necessary to understand the rationale behind these changes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For instance, some offences that are currently fine-only offences are being converted to offences which are punishable by significant jail time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These offences include, violating business stakeholding requirements, ignoring directions of the GRA, failing to give information to the GRA or failing to provide certain information to the police within a specified time frame.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The existing law already provides for heavy fines for these offences, ranging from $50,000 to over $100,000 in many cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces jail as an option, with a maximum jail term of either three years or seven years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Has there been evidence that hefty fines alone are insufficient to deter these offences and that imprisonment needs to be included?

sections.label: EP Fines and Family Visit Breaches
sections.summary: An EP can be fined up to $10,000 and jailed up to 12 months, with about five individuals yearly breaching Family Visit Limits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: An EP can be fined up to $10,000 and jailed up to 12 months if found guilty.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Based on the data shared by the Ministry, there are about five individuals each year on average that breached Family Visit Limits.

sections.label: Exclusion Order Visit Limit substitution
sections.summary: The Bill lets the NCPG and its committees immediately substitute an Exclusion Order with a Visit Limit, and vice versa, instead of waiting one to two months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With the amendment Bill, the NCPG and its committees will be able to immediately substitute an Exclusion Order with a Visit Limit, and vice versa, instead of waiting one to two months under the current legislation.

sections.label: Minors casino entry fines
sections.summary: Minors refusing to give particulars or using false evidence of age to enter casinos may be fined up to $10,000, a 10-fold increase.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Minors refusing to give particulars, such as their age, or using false evidence of age to enter casinos, may be fined up to $10,000 under the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This is a 10-fold increase from a maximum fine of $1,000 under the current regulations.

sections.label: Singapore and Macau casino tax rates
sections.summary: Singapore casino tax rates range from 8% to 12% of GGR for premium gaming and 18% to 22% for mass gaming; Macau imposes 35%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In Singapore, casino tax rates range from 8% to 12% of gross gaming revenue (GGR) for premium gaming, and 18% to 22% for mass gaming, respectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Macau, the largest gaming market globally, imposes a special gaming tax of 35% on GGR, amid other fixed and variable premiums payable, while also requiring operators to contribute a further percentage of GGR to utilities designated by the Macau government.

sections.label: Genting Singapore and Marina Bay Sands results
sections.summary: Genting Singapore's gaming revenues rose 28% to $957.6 million and Marina Bay Sands' net revenues rose 23% to US$2.17 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In their most recent half year results, Genting Singapore saw gaming revenues up 28% to $957.6 million in the first six months of the year, driving adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) 26% higher to $570.8 million and putting the company on track to beat its "robust 2023 performance", as highlighted by the company itself at its recent Annual General Meeting, where it also reported adjusted EBITDA of more than $1 billion in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Similarly, Marina Bay Sands saw net revenues up 23% in the first half of the year to US$2.17 billion, with adjusted property EBITDA up 34% to US$1.1 billion.

sections.label: MHA overlooked casino levy order expiry
sections.summary: MHA overlooked the expiry of the 2019 Order to increase casino entry levies for five years and is enacting retrospective legislation to fix the mistake.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Essentially, MHA made a mistake and overlooked the expiry of the 2019 Order to increase casino entry levies for a five-year period and is now enacting retrospective legislation to fix the mistake.

sections.label: 2019 casino entry levy increase
sections.summary: A joint press release stated casino entry levies for Singaporeans and PRs would rise 50%, with a five-year moratorium.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In the joint press release made on 3 April 2019, it was stated that "The casino entry levies for Singaporeans and PRs will be raised by 50%, from $100 to $150 for the daily levy and from $2,000 to $3,000 for the annual levy, with a five-year moratorium".

sections.label: Extra revenue and overcharged Singaporeans
sections.summary: S$4.4 million of extra revenue is meaningful but also significant to the Singaporeans or PRs who were overcharged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Yes, S$4.4 million of extra revenue is a meaningful sum, but it is also significant to the Singaporeans or PRs who were overcharged.

sections.label: Retrospective legislation for someone's mistake
sections.summary: Retrospective legislation is the exception rather than the norm, yet it is now used to make up for someone's mistake.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Given that retrospective legislation is the exception rather than the norm, why are we now using retrospective legislation to make up for someone's mistake?

sections.label: Promotional game versus casino game distinction
sections.summary: It asks whether there is reason or utility to distinguish a promotional game in a casino from casino gambling and casino games.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, relating to the distinction between promotional gambling and casino game, is there a reason or utility for distinguishing "promotional game" in the context of a casino from "casino gambling and casino games"?

sections.label: ATM prohibition within casino premises
sections.summary: It asks whether the prohibition of ATMs within casino premises is maintained on principle or for deterrence reasons.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, relating to the prohibition of automate teller machines (ATMs) within boundaries of casino premises, I would like to clarify if this law is mainly maintained on principle or are there well-grounded reasons of deterrence for this?

sections.label: Casino entry levy and visit duration
sections.summary: It supports raising the entry levy, which supports the Tote Board, and asks whether visit duration can be reduced below 24 hours.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Third, regarding increasing the cost per entry to casinos, I am in support of the increase of entry levy for both per entry period or annually and that this gives direct support to the Tote Board for public, social and charitable purposes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I wonder though whether we can tighten further and consider reducing the visit duration to less than 24 hours, for example, over 12 or 16 hours per visit.

sections.label: Third Party Exclusion Orders and reporting
sections.summary: It asks whether doctors or psychiatrists can report gambling disorder cases to the Authority and whether Courts or the Office of Public Guardian are informed of an Exclusion Order against a Donee or Deputy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Specific for Third Party Exclusion Orders, like addictions to drugs where doctors are obliged to report illicit drug abuse, can there be a mechanism where doctors or psychiatrists who find someone with a gambling disorder and puts himself, herself or others at risk of financial harm, be reported to the Authority for consideration of Third Party Exclusion Orders?

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Further to this and as a related question, is there a mechanism where the Courts or the Office of Public Guardian is informed if someone who is an existing Donee or Deputy to an incapacitated person is himself being imposed an Exclusion Order, that his suitability is reviewed with expedience and that he is not allowed to fulfil the role of Donee or Deputy, especially for property and affairs, of that incapacitated person?

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Today, I believe this only applies to undischarged bankruptcy and I wonder whether the same rule should apply, at the very least, for the duration where a person remains under an Exclusion Order, with the intent of protecting the interests of the incapacitated person to which he is Donee or Deputy to.

sections.label: Minister approval for main shareholders
sections.summary: Section 42 will be amended to require the Minister's approval, instead of GRA's approval, for divestment and acquisitions of main shareholder shareholdings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For main shareholders, section 42 will be amended to require the Minister’s approval, instead of GRA's approval, for the divestment and acquisitions of shareholdings relating to main shareholders.

sections.label: Removing hearing references
sections.summary: Sections 157, 158, 164 and 166 will be amended to remove references to a hearing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A number of provisions, including sections 157, 158, 164 and 166, will be amended to remove references to a “hearing”.

sections.label: Substituting exclusion orders and visit limits
sections.summary: New section 166A(3)(c)(iii) requires NCPG to be satisfied a substitution is in the best interests of the respondent and family members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: MHA explained that this amendment is to address the inefficient current situation where NCPG or the committee can only revoke an existing Exclusion Order or Visit Limit, and subsequently impose a new Visit Limit or Exclusion Order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 166A(3)(c)(iii) requires NPGC, before making a substitution for a third-party Exclusion Order or a Third Party Visit Limit, to be satisfied that it is in the best interests of the respondent and his or her family members.

sections.label: GRA approval for casino gambling
sections.summary: The amendment clarifies in law that GRA's approval is required for gambling activities offered in Singapore casinos, including betting and lotteries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The intent of this amendment is to future-proof our regulatory regime and to clarify in the law that GRA’s approval is required for any gambling activities offered in casinos in Singapore, including betting and lotteries.

sections.label: No cryptocurrency casino chips
sections.summary: The GRA has no intention of allowing cryptocurrency to be used as chips for casino gambling due to money laundering risks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The GRA has no intention of allowing cryptocurrency to be used as chips for casino gambling as this presents money laundering risks.

sections.label: Minister approving main shareholdings
sections.summary: The Minister, rather than the GRA, is more appropriate to approve divestments and acquisitions relating to main shareholdings to align the IRs with Singapore's strategic objectives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Members would recall that the Government's decision to develop the two IRs was based on the need to reinvent Singapore's tourism industry and the economic spin-offs such as job creation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: It is therefore more appropriate for the Minister rather than the GRA to be the authority to approve divestments and acquisitions relating to main shareholdings to ensure continued alignment between the IRs and the Singapore Government's strategic objectives.

sections.label: Casino regulation oversight rationalisation
sections.summary: Strategic whole-of-Government functions will be overseen by the Minister and regulatory functions by the GRA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Our casino operators appreciate the spirit, intent and reasons for our regulations and have a good track record in compliance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We are hence taking this opportunity to rationalise such that functions that relate to the whole-of-Government at the strategic level are overseen by the Minister and regulatory functions are overseen by the GRA.

sections.label: Casino operator information sharing
sections.summary: A new provision sets when casino operators share information directly, removing the GRA as conduit while keeping it in the loop.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The new provision stipulates the circumstances under which a casino operator has to share information with the other operator.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The GRA does not track the time taken for the current information sharing process.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: However, we believe that with the removal of the GRA as the conduit and the casino operators sharing and receiving information directly with each other, the process would be more efficient and the casino operators will be able to take timelier action, with GRA still in the loop, having visibility of the information being shared.

sections.label: Casino Control Act penalty alignment
sections.summary: Proposed amendments to the Casino Control Act align penalties with the Gambling Control Act for parity in similar offences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The proposed amendments to the Casino Control Act seek to align the penalties with the Gambling Control Act to ensure parity for similar offences.

sections.label: Resident problem gambling rates
sections.summary: Probable pathological and problem gambling rates among residents are low and stable at about 1%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: As I mentioned earlier, the probable pathological and problem gambling rates among our residents are low and stable, at about 1%.

sections.label: Office of Public Guardian suitability determination
sections.summary: The Office of Public Guardian investigates with NCPG's assistance and determines continued suitability when it knows of such a case.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: When the Office of Public Guardian comes to know of such a case, it will investigate with NCPG's assistance and make a determination of continued suitability.

sections.label: Prosecutions for exclusion breaches
sections.summary: To date, no EP has been prosecuted solely for breaching an Exclusion Order or exceeding a Visit Limit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: To date, no EP has been prosecuted solely for breaching an Exclusion Order or exceeding a Visit Limit.

sections.label: Minors using false age evidence
sections.summary: From 2019 to 2023, three minors were found to have entered a casino using false evidence of age.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In the past five years, from 2019 to 2023, three minors were found to have entered a casino using false evidence of age.

sections.label: Casino tax rates and moratorium
sections.summary: Casino tax rates were introduced in 2007 with a 15-year moratorium until 2022, and further questions can be filed with the Ministry of Finance or Ministry of Trade and Industry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: If the Member has further questions, he can file a Parliamentary Question to the Ministry of Finance or Ministry of Trade and Industry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We first introduced the casino tax rates in 2007 and introduced a 15-year moratorium until 2022.

sections.label: Tiered casino tax and moratorium expiry
sections.summary: The tiered casino tax structure and moratorium are subject to casino operators meeting development targets and expire in 2032.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The tiered casino tax structure and the moratorium are subject to the casino operators meeting development targets and they expire in 2032.

sections.label: 30-minute waiting time for deposits
sections.summary: For electronic payments by non-premium Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents into casino deposit accounts, the GRA imposed a 30-minute wait before funds are available for gambling.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Where electronic payments are used by Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents who are non-premium players to transfer funds into their deposit account with the casino operators, the GRA has imposed a 30-minute waiting time between the patron’s deposit of funds and the time that the funds are made available to the patron for gambling.

sections.label: Illegal gambling arrests in 2023
sections.summary: In 2023, the Police arrested more than 450 persons for involvement in illegal gambling activities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In 2023, the Police arrested more than 450 persons for their involvement in illegal gambling activities.

sections.label: Blocked illegal gambling websites and payments
sections.summary: Since 2015, more than 3,800 illegal gambling websites, over 270 bank accounts and more than $36 million in payments linked to illegal online gambling have been blocked.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Since 2015, we have blocked more than 3,800 illegal gambling websites, over 270 bank accounts and more than $36 million in payments linked to illegal online gambling.
